text.p: British chemicals group Albright & Wilson Plc turned in a solid half-year performance on Thursday, reporting progress in all its operations despite tough competition.

The group, which is the world's biggest producer of purified phosphoric acid -- used in products such as washing powder --lifted half-year pretax profit by 6.3 percent to 32.0 million pounds ($50 million) and its dividend by 4.7 percent to 2.25p.
It predicted "steady progress" for the rest of 1996.
Shares in the company, which have risen steadily over the past month, showed little reaction to the figures, trading unchanged at 199 pence early afternoon.

HSBC James Capel analyst David Ingles said the figures were "broadly satisfactory" and said he believed the company was on course to meet his full-year pre-tax profit forecast of 67.0 million pounds, excluding restructuring charges expected to total 3.5 million.

Sharp rises in raw material costs, which added 40 million pounds to Albright & Wilson's bills in 1995, continued to be a factor in the first six months of 1996, but chief executive Robin Paul said there were signs that prices had plateau'd.

Higher raw material costs partly offset better sales at the key phosphates division, where output includes ingredients for washing powders. Operating profits rose a modest 2.3 percent to 26.0 million pounds.

But costs at the surfactants division, whose products end up in detergents and toiletries, were relatively stable. Cost-cutting and higher sales both helped operating profits at the division to bounce by 211 percent to 5.6 milllion stg.
"We are at last getting our act together on the surfactants business," Paul told Reuters in an interview.

Another bright spot was specialty chemicals, where Albright & Wilson's customers include the water and drugs industries. Here, raw material prices fell in the first half, helping push operating profit up 7.9 percent to 8.2 million stg.

Albright & Wilson, founded in 1851, was a listed company between 1948 and 1978 and was refloated by Tenneco of the U.S. last year. It is aiming to derive at least 20 percent of sales from products under five years old, and Paul said the group has some "very effective new products" on the way, including new chemicals to stop scale from eroding water treatment systems, and flame retardants for cotton and poly-cotton fibres.
Despite spending less on research and development than many of its competitors, Paul said "If anything we are producing too many R&D ideas to have the capacity to produce them." ($1=.6412 Pound)
